rationale: fastdiff_wdm_wavelet_constrained-claude-agentic: val_n=200, seed=42, fd_recon_ckpt=/cluster/maier/Agent4CT/checkpoints/fast_diffusion_wavelet_breast.pt, fd_recon_steps=8, fd_recon_init=fbp, fd_recon_init_t=0.7, fd_recon_eta=1.0, fd_recon_dc=1, fd_recon_dc_n_cg=5, fd_recon_dc_relax=1.0, dataset_kind=breast_ct, rationale=iter-2 DC-STRENGTH lever, breast-native wavelet CONSTRAINED, val=200. SIX-BOX: (1) PRIOR: iter-1 (breast prior, init_t0.7/dc_relax0.5) scored SSIM 0.326 / PSNR 17.1 / RMSE 4.75e-2 vs 128-view sparse-FBP baseline PSNR 36.3 / RMSE 5.21e-3 -> ~9x worse, hr=0, FAR below floor and much worse than the archived Mayo-prior iter-1 (SSIM 0.72). (2) FAILURE MODE: with the CORRECTLY-scaled breast prior (out_scale 0.5), embedding the FBP at init_t=0.7 injects a large amount of prior structure that the half-strength CG DC (relax=0.5) only half-corrects back onto the measured sparse sinogram -> the strong prior at high flow-time dominates and corrupts HU. The prior is now impactful (unlike the mis-scaled Mayo prior), so weak DC is decisively wrong. (3) ONE KNOB: fd_recon_dc_relax 0.5 -> 1.0 (full CG-projected-image blend), all else identical to iter-1. (4) HYPOTHESIS: at dc_relax=1.0 the recon leans fully on the CG solve of min||Ax-y||^2 onto the measured sinogram each step, so RMSE drops sharply toward the sparse-FBP floor (the archived Mayo-prior curve gained SSIM 0.72->0.82 on exactly this knob at iter-2, and dc_relax=1.0 was best throughout). FALSIFIER: if RMSE stays >>baseline, the high init_t is the dominant problem -> iter-3 lowers init_t to 0.4 (the archived best region). (5) BUDGET: iter-1 ran ~90s for 200 slices; dc_relax is free. (6) Loop continues; iter-3 self-dispatched on landing.
